title: Culture Dish
summary: Scan falling specimens for order and degree, then set a growth lamp and a spring from dy/dt = ky and y″ + m²y = 0.
subject: mathematics
ncertRef: Section 9.2, Order and degree of a differential equation
concepts: Degree and when it is not defined
learningOutcome: The student can read the order and degree of a differential equation, know when the degree is not defined, and use the solutions of dy/dt = ky and y″ + m²y = 0 to set a constant.

levels.title: Order and degree
levels.adds: Baseline: order is the highest derivative; degree is its power when the equation is polynomial in its derivatives, else not defined (Ex 9.1 Q1 to Q12).
hints: Find the highest derivative: its order is the order of the equation.
Look at the power of that highest derivative only.
A derivative inside sin, cos or e means the degree is not defined.

levels.title: Growth and decay
levels.adds: New: dy/dt = k·y separates to y = c·e^(kt); the reading after a time fixes k (Ex 9.3 Q19 to Q22; Example 9).
hints: Separate: dy/y = k dt, then integrate both sides.
Use y = c at t = 0 to get y = c·e^(kt).
Put t = T and match the exponent to get k.

levels.title: The spring
levels.adds: New: y″ + m²y = 0 has the solution y = A cos(mt) + B sin(mt), with period 2π/m (Section 9.3; Ex 9.2 Q1 to Q10).
hints: Check that y = cos(mt) satisfies y″ = −m²y.
In a turn of 2π the dish makes m full swings.

misconceptions: The degree is the highest power anywhere in the equation
Every differential equation has a degree
A bigger k always means a bigger colony
